newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's MTRC revolving credit raised to HK$5.0 bln.
newsitem.headline: HK's MTRC revolving credit raised to HK$5.0 bln.

text.p: The Mass Transit Railway Corp's five-year revolving credit facility has been increased to HK$5.0 billion from HK$3.5 billion in syndication, the MTRC said on Wednesday.
The facility attracted total subscriptions of more than HK$5.5 billion but the MTRC said it decided to increase the amount to HK$5.0 billion only.
The interest margin of the facility is 36.5 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.
Twenty-three banks and financial institutions joined the 12 arrangers and underwriters in the deal. Signing is scheduled to take place on January 6.

Arrangers are Chase Manhattan Asia, Hang Seng Bank, Industrial Bank of Japan Hong Kong branch, BA Asia, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, Bayerische Landesbank Hong Kong branch, Deutsche Bank Hong Kong branch, Fuji Bank, JP Morgan Securities Asia, Paribas Asia, Sanwa Bank Hong Kong branch and Union Bank of Switzerland.

Co-arrangers are ABN AMRO Bank, Asahi Bank Hong Kong branch, Banca Commerciale Italiana Hong Kong branch, Bank of Nova Scotia, Banque Nationale de Paris Hong Kong branch, CIBC CEF, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank Hong Kong branch, DG Bank Deutsche Genossenschaftsbank Hong Kong branch, Dresdner Bank Hong Kong branch, Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan, Sakura Bank, Standard Chartered Bank and Tokai Bank Hong Kong branch.
Co-lead managers are Bank of Yokohama Hong Kong branch, Kwong On Bank, Mitsubishi Trust and Banking Corp Hong Kong branch, Shanghai Commercial Bank and Toyo Trust and Banking Co Hong Kong branch.
Senior managers are Banca di Roma SpA Hong Kong branch, Nikko Merchant Bank (Singapore), Sumitomo Bank and Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co Hong Kong branch.
